Keep Failing Pupils Back Tories From Bbc Online

Sep 2, 2007 • Janice Cotcher

“Failing students should repeat the last year of primary school, British Tory leader David Cameron has proposed.”
Last Updated: Sunday, 2 September 2007, 15:02 GMT 16:02 UK

I can see the benefits of keeping a student with their peer group but I’m not sure it outweighs the benefits of repeating a grade. As a high school teacher, I too often see students fall further and further behind because the basic skills are just not there. I believe not holding back students back is a big part why we have so many high school students who cannot even read or write at a Grade 5 level (don’t even get me started on the math skills). There is a stigma of being “left behind” but often these students are immature and may benefit of socializing with a younger peer group (which I have seen).

Right now in the current system, all a teacher can do is recommend that a student be held back until the senior grades. The ultimate decision for repetition lies with the parent/ guardian. Some students are recommend to be held back year after year only to be undeservingly promoted. I see how helpless teachers feel; it completely takes their power away.

I agree with the UK Schools Minister that earlier intervention than Grade 6 is needed but something has to be done. What are his ideas for earlier intervention? The current system is not working. I think sometimes you have to go with the best idea until a better one presents itself. Decisions on shaping the future of a nation is not something you can postpone.

Another point: what are the students learning by being promoted not on their own merits? Failure can be a valuable educational experience. Shouldn’t we be teaching students how to overcome their failures? Shouldn’t we teach them the importance of the end product rather than working the system?
